byTitle.Tesla Pulls Model Y AWD Trim, Premium So: Tesla has removed the $41,990 Model Y AWD from its U.S. order page, leaving the $39,990 RWD as the entry model and the $49,990 Premium AWD as the cheapest all-wheel-drive version. Premium orders now show January–March 2027 delivery estimates; Tesla has not said whether the trim is gone for good.
byTitle.Tesla FSD Supervised at NZ Expo: 5 Detai: Tesla Australia & New Zealand will offer FSD (Supervised) demo rides in a Model 3 RWD at the NZ EV & Tech Expo in Auckland on 13–15 November 2026. FSD has been subscription-only in New Zealand at NZ$159 a month since 31 March 2026, and Tesla’s September safety data cited 160 million km driven on it across Australia and New Zealand.
byTitle.Elon Musk Could Announce Tesla-SpaceX Me: IBD relays Bloomberg’s report that Tesla and SpaceX could announce a merger as soon as December, with early 2027 also discussed, while boards and advisers work through terms and governance. No agreement has been reached, and a deal would likely need a separate Tesla shareholder vote.
byTitle.SpaceX-Tesla Merger Could Come Soon: Wha: Yahoo Finance looks at what Tesla and SpaceX holders might receive in a combination now reported to be progressing toward a possible December announcement. No exchange ratio or valuation has been agreed; reports say the talks centre on how many SpaceX shares Tesla investors would get.
byTitle.Tesla Stock Best Run in a Year on SpaceX: Benzinga says Tesla shares posted their best five-day rally in more than a year, up about 16% since the 5 November close and adding roughly $218 billion of market value, as merger talks with SpaceX were reported to be progressing. A deal could be announced as early as December but may slip into early 2027.
byTitle.SpaceX and Tesla advance merger talks to: CNBC reports on Bloomberg’s story that SpaceX and Tesla are advancing merger negotiations toward what would be the largest deal ever. Reports put the combined value at roughly $3.4–3.5 trillion, with a December announcement possible and early 2027 an alternative.
byTitle.SpaceX and Tesla Talks on Record Merger: Bloomberg reports that Tesla and SpaceX are progressing in merger negotiations and could announce the biggest-ever deal as soon as December, though an announcement could slip into early 2027. Boards and advisers are working out the terms and the governance structure of the combined company, with ring-fencing Tesla’s China business from SpaceX’s defense work among the issues.
byTitle.If You Want to Order a New Tesla Cybertr: Tesla has removed the Dual Motor AWD and Premium AWD Cybertruck versions from its order site, leaving only the tri-motor Cyberbeast from $112,235 including order and destination fees. The change follows Musk’s plan to end Cybertruck production in 2027 to make room for Cybercab.
byTitle.House Republican invites Musk to move Te: Rep. Carlos Giménez (R-Fla.) sent Elon Musk a letter inviting him to move Tesla’s headquarters from Austin to Florida, citing concerns about politically motivated investigations in Texas after the midterms. He pitched South Florida’s workforce, infrastructure and business climate; Tesla has not responded publicly.
byTitle.SpaceX-Tesla merger: 3 things to know ab: Quartz notes that no terms have been agreed and that a combined SpaceX–Tesla would be worth about $3.5 trillion at current prices. Musk is excluded from the special committees but holds roughly 82% of SpaceX’s voting power and about 20% of Tesla, which reports say could leave him with around 56% voting control of a combined company.
byTitle.Why SpaceX Stock Is Getting in the Way o: Barron’s (paywalled) argues that SpaceX’s share price is complicating the terms of a stock-for-stock Tesla deal; a summary of the piece says it cites a “political discount” of up to 25% on SpaceX shares. A weaker SpaceX price means more SpaceX shares would have to be issued to Tesla holders.
byTitle.If SpaceX and Tesla Merge, Here's What a: The Motley Fool argues that a $10,000 stake in a combined SpaceX–Tesla is more likely to be worth less by 2030 than more, despite bullish scenarios. It says a roughly $3.5 trillion combined valuation is hard to justify given Tesla’s slow growth and both companies’ high multiples.
byTitle.Tesla extending Cybertruck production th: CBS reports Musk’s statement that Cybertruck production will continue through the end of summer 2027 to work through the order backlog, later than the mid-2027 wind-down he announced on 6 November. Tesla may still have to refund deposits for orders it cannot build before the line closes.
byTitle.Tesla (TSLA) Forms Special Committee To: A Simply Wall St piece on Yahoo Finance notes that Tesla and SpaceX have each formed special committees of independent directors to evaluate a potential all-stock merger. It says the next proof point would be a deal framework with valuation, an exchange ratio and a separate vote for Tesla’s outside shareholders.
byTitle.Finland clears Tesla assisted driving te: Reuters reports that Finland has approved Tesla’s FSD (Supervised) driver-assistance software after changes were made to the system. Tesla’s Q3 update said FSD was already available in nine EU countries before this approval.
